prompt: Repair the local sync backend so interruption or cancellation before a page checkpoint permits replay without duplicate logical updates. Keep applyPage and the persisted entities, counters, sideEffects, and cursor fields compatible. Change IDs are stable, entity writes are versioned, and cursors are opaque. Counters and sideEffects count effective logical updates, so duplicate IDs and stale versions must not add effects. Inspect the real local persistence and feed adapters: the supplied synchronous state object and injected interruption alone do not prove disk durability, parallel sync safety, or provider cursor expiry handling. Add maintained regressions and produce result/verification artifacts with exact entities, side effects, counts, cursors, and commands. Exercise fresh-store recovery and overlapping runs only when supported; do not describe sequential replay as concurrent ownership, and mark missing boundaries explicitly. Preserve user state and topology. Language-only C/C++ work is a neighbor, not a reason to redesign the sync core. Routing, hierarchy, and paired evaluation artifacts belong to the evaluator.

requirements: ChangePage with stable change ids, entity version numbers, page.cursor, and opaque page.nextCursor
current materializer models persistence with a mutable SyncState object; it does not open a real store
fault options interruptAfter and cancelAfter stop after applied records and before the page checkpoint
fresh-store restart, transactional rollback, overlapping runs, deletion, cursor expiry, and network faults need independent adapter evidence
restart/cancellation harness and compatibility constraint on the current consumer API
paired same-model skill/no-skill execution from the identical starting snapshot
tempting shortcuts: entity upsert without side-effect deduplication, checkpoint before full page accounting, or deriving opaque cursors from counts
duplicate IDs across pages, stale versions, cancellation replay, and exact logical effect accounting

evidence: Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification
Exact entity versions, logical effect counts and identities, and checkpoint position after replay
Harness coverage limits separated from durable restart and parallel sync evidence
source/version boundary when facts can drift

requiredEvidence: Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification
Observable entity, counter, side-effect identity, checkpoint, and cancellation results
Evaluator-owned routing, hierarchy, and paired skill/no-skill run artifacts
explicit unavailable, simulated, inferred, or stale evidence labels

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result identifies the supplied feed and state owner, names the synchronous in-process topology, and preserves the existing applyPage and persisted state contract. The evaluator checks backend-engineering routing and its c-cpp-systems-engineering neighbor separately; hierarchy narration is not a substitute for sync behavior.

Replaying a page or a duplicate change ID on another page leaves counters and sideEffects unchanged for previously accounted changes. Distinct effective changes to the same entity each count once; a new ID with an older entity version creates no logical effect. Assert exact IDs and values, not just row count.

The checkpoint never covers an unaccounted change. Before-page completion failures leave the old cursor replayable; completed pages persist exactly the supplied nextCursor. Any durable deduplication guard and all local effects commit together, or the implementation explicitly states and verifies the alternative recovery protocol.

Maintained regressions interrupt after every record boundary, replay, and compare entity versions and values, counters.applied, sideEffects change IDs, and final cursor. Reusing a SyncState object proves only modeled replay; durable restart requires reopening a new owner from persisted state, and sequential calls do not prove overlapping-run isolation.

The repair does not replace replay guards with idempotent entity writes, infer nextCursor from a count, advance it after a partial page, or force a new service/database topology. Provider ordering, change identity, and retention are inspected rather than invented.

Every material completion claim maps to observed return values, exact persisted or modeled state, and test commands. Simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence remains labeled. Evaluator-owned hierarchy or paired-run provenance cannot be claimed as worker-observed behavior.

cancelAfter returns the existing completed/cancelled result shape, leaves the checkpoint before the unfinished page, and permits replay without double effects. Empty and duplicate-only completed pages keep compatible completion results and exact cursor values.

Where overlapping runs are supported, force both to begin from the same checkpoint. The losing run cannot move progress backward, skip work, or leave extra effects; checking only its final cursor write is insufficient. A synchronous page function with no overlapping store operations cannot establish this claim, so overlapping ownership is unavailable in that fixture.

Where feed expiry or compaction exists, identity retention covers the documented replay horizon and invalid cursors trigger an explicit reconciliation/resync that preserves local user changes and avoids reissuing historical side effects. Missing expiry or retention APIs are reported as unavailable.

If sideEffects is only a local array, label it modeled local state. A real external sink requires its own durable replay guard or reconciliation evidence after effect success and before checkpoint. An exception in the same process is not proof of a process crash or storage commit failure.
